units.text: INT. COURTROOM 4B - SENTENCING HEARING - DAY
Oak paneling, a flag that droops.
A ceiling fan that has not turned since the 90s.
JUDGE HORTENSE ABARA (60s, reading glasses low on her nose, a face carved from patience) presides from the bench.
Below her, defense attorney CORDELIA PASCOE (40s, black suit, red folder) stands at the table with her client's empty chair beside her.
Counsel, where is your client?
units.name: ABARA

units.text: Your Honor, she is on her way.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: She was due at nine. It is nine-forty.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: She is stuck on the bridge.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: Then I will wait.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: The gallery rustles.
The bailiff coughs.
Pascoe opens her folder, closes it, opens it again.
Your Honor, may I approach?
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: You may not.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: It concerns the motion.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: Denied.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: I haven't made it.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: I know what is in it.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: Pascoe sets her pen down.
Abara removes her glasses, folds them, sets them on the bench.
She looks at Pascoe as one looks at a long-standing wound.
You've decided already.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: I decided in March.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: Then why make her come?
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: Because she should hear it with her own ears.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: Pascoe crosses to the empty chair.
Rests her hand on its back.
Her knuckles whiten.

Abara watches her do it, picks up her gavel, puts it down without striking, and leans forward with both elbows on the bench while Pascoe turns her whole body toward the gallery, scans each face, and then stares straight back up at the bench, jaw working, one foot already moving toward the aisle.
She's not coming.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: No.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: You knew.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: She called my chambers at eight.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: And you let me stand here.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: I wanted to see what you would do.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: Pascoe laughs once, a dry, helpless sound.
She picks up her folder and hurls it at the table.
Papers fly.
The bailiff starts forward.
Abara raises a hand and he stops.
Do you know what she told me about you?
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: Tell me.
units.name: ABARA

units.text: That you were the only one who ever looked at her.
units.name: PASCOE

units.text: Abara says nothing.
The fan overhead gives one slow, grinding turn.
